specific_rules: Steel angles and plates to be NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted in design documents.
Channels to be NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted.
Steel W shapes (I sections) and tees to be NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted.
Structural steel shall conform to requirements listed on Structural General Notes, including any local subgrade requirements.
Steel subgrade for members to be documented per individual structure or component in steel subcontractor's information.

Selection of subgrade for connection fittings and subcontractor-designed items to comply with NBN EN 1993-1-10 and Belgian National Annex; coordinate with SER if subcontractor details conflict with indicative subgrade in SER notes.
Steel sections for general metal fabrications to comply with EN 10025.
Steel sections for stairs and stringers to comply with EN 10025.
Hollow structural sections to be NBN EN 10210 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted in design documents.
Hot finished steel structural hollow sections for general fabrications to comply with EN 10210.
Hot finished hollow sections for stairs and ramps to comply with EN 10210.
Cold-formed welded structural hollow sections, where used, to comply with ISO 10799.

materials.grade_or_type: S350 to NBN EN 10346 / NBN EN 10143
specific_rules: Deck units and sheet accessories to be produced from galvanized steel sheet conforming to NBN EN 10346 and NBN EN 10143, Grade of steel S350 unless indicated or agreed otherwise.
Deck units shall be free of materials such as dirt, rust and rolling oils that are detrimental to bond of finishes to be field applied.
Roof deck shall be wide rib units and shall have no stiffening ribs in the top surface.

Shear stud connectors to be proprietary type complying with EN ISO 13918 (or BS EN ISO 13918), with minimum yield strength of 350 N/mm², minimum ultimate tensile strength of 450 N/mm² and minimum elongation of 15%.
Stud shear connectors for steel decking to comply with EN ISO 13918 with same minimum strength and elongation requirements.
Stud size and spacing to be as specified by Engineer of Record for composite action and diaphragm requirements.
Shear connectors to be shop welded using automatic end welding in accordance with manufacturer’s printed instructions and surfaces prepared as recommended by the connector manufacturer.

materials.grade_or_type: Grade 8.8; NBN EN 1090 / EN ISO 898 / NBN EN 14399
specific_rules: Bolts, nuts and washers for primary structural connections to comply with NBN EN 1090 requirements and to be Grade 8.8 unless otherwise noted on design documents.
High-strength bolts to conform to provisions of NBN EN 1993 and NBN EN 14399 for preloaded assemblies.
Bolts, nuts and washers for metal fabrications to comply with EN ISO 898 for mechanical properties.
All bolts shall be new and not re-used in structural applications.
High-strength bolted assemblies for bearing-type connections to be designed assuming threads included in the shear plane unless specified otherwise.
Slip-critical connections (moment connections and bracing) to use direct tension indicator washers or tension control bolted assemblies installed per manufacturer’s written instructions.
Bolts for non-preloaded structural connections to comply with NBN EN 15048 where specified.
Anchor bolts to comply with NBN EN 15048 with grade as specified in design documents.
Anchor bolts to be non-headed type unless indicated otherwise on drawings.
Post-installed anchors to comply with requirements in Structural General Notes.
Contractor to accurately survey location, alignment and elevation of anchor rods prior to erection; discrepancies to be reported and corrected before steel erection commences.
Structural steel erection shall not commence until any anchor misalignment issues are corrected.
Welding materials to comply with NBN EN 1090 and associated welding standards appropriate to the steel grade being welded.
Welding electrodes for structural steel to conform to relevant standards listed under reference standards; specifically Group 5 of NBN EN 1993-1-8 for electrode classification.
Welding materials for metal fabrications to comply with EN 1011 recommendations.
Welders performing work on steel deck and structural steel to be qualified according to NBN EN ISO 9606-1; qualification to be within the previous 12 months.
Welders performing shear stud welding to be certified by recognised authority in project location.
Qualification of welding operators and weld setters for mechanized/automatic welding to comply with NBN EN ISO 14732 where applicable.

materials.grade_or_type: Non-shrink, non-metallic; 35 MPa at 28 days (strength ignored per instructions, but type kept)
specific_rules: Grout for column base plates and similar interfaces to be non-shrink and non-metallic aggregate type.
Grout to be compatible with steel baseplates and installed in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.
Contractor to refer to Structural General Notes and Drawings for specific grout locations and details.
Grout to be placed solidly between column plates and bearing surfaces and trowelled smooth with 45-degree splay at edges.

materials.grade_or_type: Rust inhibitive primer; inorganic zinc-rich primer where required
specific_rules: Fabricator’s standard grey rust inhibitive primer to be used for shop and touch-up priming, complying with VOC limitations of the authorities having jurisdiction.
Touch-up primer for galvanized surfaces to be the fabricator’s standard compatible with galvanizing and complying with VOC limits.
Members exposed to exterior outside of a controlled building environment to receive inorganic zinc-rich primer with at least 60% volume solids and at least 85% metallic zinc in the dry film.
Surfaces receiving intumescent paint to receive a heavy duty alkyd primer compatible with the selected intumescent coating system.
For intumescent systems, primers such as Sherwin Williams FIRETEX C69 to be applied with nominal DFT 25 microns (as defined by EN ISO 12944-5) unless otherwise specified by manufacturer.
Primer coats for intumescent systems must be fully cured and compatible with intumescent topcoats per manufacturer’s certification.
Slab edge pour stops, edge strips, closure strips and sump pans to be formed from minimum 1.6 mm steel.
Fillers, ridge and valley plates, sheet metal closures and necessary supports at openings, columns and penetrations to be formed from minimum 0.8 mm steel sheet.
Closures for openings in metal deck 1.58 mm wide and over to include cover plates, column closures, sheet metal collars and ridge/valley plates as necessary for roofing interface.
Necessary steel framing to be provided for deck support at columns and openings, coordinated with structural steel framing.

materials.category: Mechanical and Sidelap Fasteners for Deck
materials.grade_or_type: Proprietary (e.g., Hilti) mechanical fasteners and sidelap connectors
specific_rules: Mechanical fasteners for metal deck attachment and sidelap connectors may be proprietary systems such as Hilti or other approved alternatives.
Alternative mechanical anchoring systems for metal deck must be supported by submitted and approved diaphragm calculations demonstrating adequacy.

Self-tapping screws used for longitudinal side lap connections must be of minimum size specified (nominal 3.0 mm diameter class, described as 'Size 300 mm' in text) and spaced as per installation rules.
Sheet metal screws are not permitted for longitudinal edge closure fastening; closures must be tack welded at specified spacing.

materials.grade_or_type: EN 10025 sections, EN 10210 hollow sections, ISO 3574/6317 plates, ISO 4200 pipe
specific_rules: Steel sections for metal fabrications to comply with EN 10025.
Steel hollow sections for metal fabrications to comply with EN 10210.
Steel plates for fabrications to comply with ISO 3574 and ISO 6317 as applicable.
Steel pipe for barrier rails and miscellaneous items to comply with ISO 4200.
Ungalvanized steel sheet to be hot or cold-rolled, with cold-rolled used where finished work is exposed to view.
Hot-rolled sheet to comply with ISO 4995; cold-rolled sheet to comply with ISO 4997.

materials.grade_or_type: EN 10025 sections, ISO 4200 pipe, ISO 10799 tubing, EN 10088 stainless where needed
specific_rules: Steel sections for stairs and ramps to comply with EN 10025.
Steel tubing for handrails and guards to comply with ISO 10799 for structural tubing.
Pipe for handrails and guards to comply with ISO 4200.
Stainless steel, where specified, to comply with EN 10088, particularly grade 1.4436 where used.
Bar grating for treads and ramps to comply with NAAMM MBG 531 or MBG 532, whichever applies.

Materials for fixed ladders, handrails and guards to be manufacturer’s standard steel tubes, plates, bars, shapes, sheets, wire and mesh complying with material article of section and appropriate standards.

materials.grade_or_type: Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX2003 / FX6002 systems
specific_rules: Intumescent coatings to be factory-mixed, single pack thin-film formulations for spray application.

System 1: Solvent-based product for internal steelwork (C1) off-site application, comprising FIRETEX FX2003 intumescent coating with DFT per fire resistance requirement, FIRETEX C69 primer at nominal 25 microns DFT as per EN ISO 12944-5, and FIRETEX M71V2 sheen finish top sealer coat at nominal 50 microns DFT as per EN ISO 12944-5.

System 2: Solvent-based product for internal steelwork (C1) off-site application, comprising FIRETEX FX6002 ultra fast drying intumescent coating with DFT per fire resistance requirement, FIRETEX C69 primer at nominal 25 microns DFT and FIRETEX M71V2 sheen finish top sealer coat at nominal 50 microns DFT.

Under certain circumstances FIRETEX FX2003 may be applied directly to steel blast-cleaned to minimum Sa 2.5 per EN ISO 8501-1 with surface profile 50–100 microns; use only when approved by manufacturer’s Technical Sales Department.
A/E of Record is to adjust intumescent system DFT build-up for alternate environment classifications (C2, C3, C4, etc.) based on EN ISO 12944 and manufacturer guidance.
Product certificates must document compatibility of intumescent coatings with existing primers, adhesives and other coatings on steel substrates.

materials.category: Barrier Rails, Ladders and Miscellaneous Fabrications
specific_rules: Ladders to be steel with mounting brackets and attachments, galvanized after fabrication, rails/stiles as manufacturer’s standard steel flat bars with eased edges and spacing not more than 600 mm, rungs 20–50 mm rectangular steel, maximum 600 mm width, and vertical spacing 225–300 mm, consistent per flight.
Ladder rungs to be spaced 175 mm clear from wall surface, fitted into side rails, plug welded and ground smooth on outer faces.

Ladder supports to be welded or bolted steel brackets designed to hold ladder minimum 175 mm clear of wall, with intermediate supports not more than 1500 mm apart, subject to Structural Engineer calculations.
Ladder rails to extend minimum 1100 mm above top rung and return to wall or structure; goose-neck extended rails where structure does not extend above top rung.
Safety cage hoops to be provided above 3 m from finished floor level where shown.
Barrier rails to be fabricated from 40 mm diameter steel pipe and steel channel sections with galvanized finish.

Concrete edge confinement angles to be steel angles with galvanized finish, with integral anchor bolts welded to angles with 2.5 mm full-perimeter fillet welds, anchorages not greater than 1200 mm on center, and angle legs mitre-cut at corners.
Roof opening framing, downpipe guards, cantilevered canopy supports and similar items to be as detailed, with prime paint or galvanized finish as specified.

finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: Sa 2.5 to EN ISO 8501-1; EN ISO 8503-1; EN ISO 8503-2; EN ISO 8502-3
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Ensure structural steel complies with Sa 2.5 cleanliness at time of blasting with initial rust grade A or B; use suitable abrasives free from fines, water and oil; remove abrasive residues and surface defects detrimental to protective paint system; blast only when relative humidity is below 85% and steel surface temperature is at least 3 °C above dew point; remove all traces of blast residue and dust; require workers to wear clean gloves when handling blast-cleaned steel; surface profile ranges and dust contamination to comply with EN ISO 8503-2 and EN ISO 8502-3 for intumescent and paint system acceptance.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Corrosion Protection – Paint Systems for Structural Steel
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: NBN EN ISO 12944-1; NBN EN ISO 12944-2; NBN EN ISO 12944; EN ISO 12944-5
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Apply corrosion protection painting to all primary steelwork unless noted otherwise to NBN EN ISO 12944; adopt corrosivity classifications C2 for internal steelwork and C4 for external steelwork unless overridden by specific project documentation; ensure compatibility between corrosion protection system and intumescent paint systems; submit proposals indicating durability ranges (L, M, H, VH) in line with clause 5.5 of NBN EN ISO 12944-1; ensure coating materials are recommended by manufacturers for the specific surface and exposure conditions and are mutually compatible; during shop application, check thickness of each coat with wheel or comb gauge in accordance with NBN EN ISO 2808; avoid coating defects such as slumping, cracking, flaking, blistering, chalking, discolouration or loss of gloss over service life; ensure finishes are uniform in texture, colour and appearance within accepted samples.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Galvanizing – Structural Steel and Metal Fabrications
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: EN ISO 1461; NBN EN ISO 1461; EN ISO 14713-1
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Complete all cutting, welding and drilling before galvanizing; design fabrications to minimise risk of distortion and to be suitable for galvanizing; provide all necessary vent and drain holes of correct size and in approved locations and seal after galvanizing; where there is concern about distortion of large articles, consider single-dipping and, where single-dip is not possible, consider splicing the structure; all galvanizing to comply with EN ISO 1461 requirements; consider design guidance and corrosion resistance principles in EN ISO 14713-1; galvanize structural steel members for metal fabrications after fabrication; galvanize items to be embedded in concrete or masonry; galvanize external handrails, stairs, ramps, ladders, barrier rails, ledge and shelf angles supporting metal decking and downspout guards as specified.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Shop Priming – Structural Steel and Fabrications
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: NBN EN ISO 12944; EN ISO 8503-1; EN ISO 17463; EN ISO 12944-5
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Apply specified shop coat of grey rust inhibitive primer in accordance with manufacturer’s product data within four hours after surface cleaning and before rust-bloom occurs; apply only when relative humidity is below 85% and steel surface temperature is at least 3 °C above dew point; for structural steel, paint all members with a shop coat except members encased in concrete, surfaces in contact with concrete, contact surfaces of welded connections and within 50 mm of field welds, contact surfaces of slip-critical high-strength bolted connections, surfaces receiving sprayed-on or intumescent fireproofing (where alternative compatible primers are specified) and surfaces receiving field-welded steel studs; during application, verify coating thickness with appropriate gauges to EN ISO 2808; for metal fabrications and stairs, prime paint with one coat grey metal primer or approved equal to minimum 50 microns DFT; do not prime surfaces that are in direct contact with concrete or require site welding; clean surfaces of rust, scale, grease and foreign matter prior to priming; touch up abraded galvanized areas and unprimed surfaces on site with specified touch-up primer for galvanized surfaces complying with EN ISO 17463; external metal fabrications and stairs/ramps to be pre-finished in factory to a finish suitable for a C4 environment in accordance with EN ISO 12944-2:2017 and ISO 9223:2012.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Inorganic Zinc-Rich Priming for External Structural Steel
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: For members exposed to the exterior outside of a controlled building environment, use inorganic zinc-rich primer with minimum 60% volume solids and producing minimum 85% metallic zinc in the dried film; apply over correctly prepared steel surfaces (Sa 2.5) and verify DFT and coating integrity in accordance with EN ISO 12944-5 and manufacturer’s instructions.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Intumescent Fire Protection – FIRETEX FX2003 System
finishes_and_protection.environment_class: C1 internal (off-site application); adaptable to C2–C4 by A/E
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: EN 16623; EN 13381; EN 13501; EN ISO 12944-5; Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX2003; FIRETEX C69; FIRETEX M71V2
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Prime steel with Sherwin Williams FIRETEX C69 Fast Track Blast Primer at nominal 25 microns DFT as defined by EN ISO 12944-5 on blast-cleaned steel to at least Sa 2.5 (EN ISO 8501-1) with surface profile 50–100 microns; in some cases FIRETEX FX2003 may be applied directly to blast-cleaned steel under manufacturer guidance; apply FIRETEX FX2003 intumescent coating to the DFT required to achieve specified fire resistance ratings in accordance with EN 13381 test data and assessments; apply top sealer coat FIRETEX M71V2 Sheen Finish at nominal 50 microns DFT as defined by EN ISO 12944-5; ensure full compatibility between primer, intumescent and topcoat; protect applied coatings from rain, direct sunlight, high humidity and wind-borne contamination during application, drying and curing; do not apply additional coats until previous layers have fully cured; adjust total DFT and system selection where environment classifications differ from C1 (e.g., C2, C3, C4) based on A/E instructions and manufacturer guidance.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Intumescent Fire Protection – FIRETEX FX6002 System
finishes_and_protection.environment_class: C1 internal (off-site application); adaptable to other classes
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: EN 16623; EN 13381; EN 13501; EN ISO 12944-5; Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX6002; FIRETEX C69; FIRETEX M71V2
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Prime steel with FIRETEX C69 Fast Track Blast Primer at nominal 25 microns DFT; apply Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX6002 ultra fast drying intumescent coating to DFT required to achieve fire resistance ratings specified on drawings using EN 13381-4 based assessment; apply FIRETEX M71V2 sheen finish top sealer coat at nominal 50 microns DFT; follow same environmental and curing controls as for FX2003 system; adjust DFTs if environment class differs from baseline C1, in accordance with A/E of Record and manufacturer recommendations.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: External Handrails, Stairs and Ramps Corrosion Protection
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: All external handrail, stair and ramp installations and associated components are to be pre-finished in factory to a finish suitable for C4 corrosivity category per EN ISO 12944-2:2017 and ISO 9223:2012; hot-dip galvanize all external components in accordance with EN ISO 1461; prepare steel substrates prior to coating according to coating manufacturers’ requirements; number of primer coats to achieve minimum 50 microns DFT as base prior to any additional topcoat systems where specified.

All external and exposed metal fabrications and associated components to be pre-finished in factory to a finish suitable for C4 environment per EN ISO 12944-2:2017 and ISO 9223:2012; structural steel members to be hot-dip galvanized to EN ISO 1461 where specified and then, if required, overcoated with appropriate paint systems assessed for anticorrosive properties according to EN ISO 17463; touch up abraded galvanized areas after fabrication using specified touch-up primer for galvanised surfaces; ensure joints exposed to weather are fabricated to exclude water or incorporate weep holes where water may accumulate.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Finish Quality Requirements for External Steel Structures
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: The finish on external steel structures must satisfy the requirement for a 'bright, light surface' in terms of relative absorptivity as per NBN EN 1991-1-5 to comply with design assumptions on solar gain and temperature effects on steelwork.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Structural Steel Design and Connection Detailing
tolerances_and_rules: All structural steelwork on the project is to be executed to Execution Class 2 (EXC2) as defined by NBN EN 1090-2 unless otherwise noted on A/E drawings.

Connections not detailed on the drawings are to be designed by the Contractor’s Engineer under direct supervision of a Professional Structural Engineer with Chartered/PE level experience in similar work.
Design and detail connections to resist loads and reactions shown in design documents and at least those required for robustness by NBN EN 1991; include proper account of eccentricities in design.

Beam-to-column connections to minimise eccentric loading on columns; unrestrained simple beam end connections to be detailed and fabricated to minimise or eliminate end restraint; welds, bolts and connection material to be designed including eccentricity effects.

Beams to be designed for end shear reactions shown in design documents; bracing connections to be designed for forces indicated; all members’ connections to be designed for relevant actions in project documents.

Except for moment connections and bracing, provide high-strength bearing-type bolted connections designed assuming threads included in shear plane; for moment connections and bracing, use slip-critical bolted connections with direct tension indicators or tension control assemblies.
Members forming bracing systems or lattice girders to be positioned such that their lines of action intersect at a common point unless detailed otherwise.
All connection and detail drawings to be prepared under supervision of the Contractor’s Engineer in accordance with NBN EN 1993.
Contractor must design and provide any stiffener plates, doubler plates, reinforcing plates and their connections necessary to transfer forces and satisfy connection criteria from Contract Documents.

All forces shown on drawings to be assumed reversible unless noted; connections must be checked for both directions; where no forces are shown, assume critical combinations of member forces for design.

For high restraint welds, use double bevels instead of single where practicable; detail joints to accommodate weld shrinkage; show welding sequence in drawings for plates in more than one plane; generally start welding at most restrained parts and progress to least restrained.

Connection design calculation packages must use a logical numbering system; resubmittals to maintain numbers with 'R' suffix; all changes to be clouded; alternative numbering can be mandated by BIM Execution Plan or project documentation.

Provide sketches for each calculation clearly showing geometry, pitch, gauge, edge distances, unbraced lengths and Whitmore length assumptions; sketches must be to scale with enough variants to cover full range of conditions.
For repetitive connections, provide summary spreadsheets or program output with link to a standard parent calculation.
Provide drawings locating each connection type keyed to its calculation reference.
Calculations may be typed, spreadsheet-based or computer-generated; spreadsheets must show inputs and results for every step with explanatory text and sketches of assumptions.
Provide explicit calculation checks for all forces shown on drawings in accordance with NBN EN 1993; 'OK by inspection' is not acceptable.
Connection design and detailing are subject to review and comment by Engineer of Record but such review does not relieve fabricator’s engineer of full professional responsibility.
Shop fabricate structural steel to the greatest extent possible to minimise field splicing and assembly.
Identify and record materials and components using methods submitted for approval; marks must remain visible for checking after erection but not on exposed faces, subject to Architect approval.
Fabricate steel members in a delivery sequence that expedites erection and minimises handling on site.
Complete full assembly, including all unit welding, prior to commencement of finishing operations where a finish is required; exposed member surfaces to be free of markings, burrs and defects.
Shop connections to be welded or bolted as indicated; field connections to be bolted except where welded or other connections are specifically indicated.
Provide high-strength threaded fasteners for principal bolted connections unless unfinished bolts are indicated for secondary framing.
Use unfinished threaded fasteners only for connections of secondary framing (purlins, girts, members taking only nominal stresses) and temporary bracing.
High-strength threaded fasteners to be installed in accordance with NBN EN 14399 and NBN EN 15048 with hardened washers under the turned element to facilitate inspection of tightening.
Welded construction to comply with NBN EN 1090, including inspection, testing and acceptance requirements; welding to follow EN 1011 recommendations.
Assemble and weld built-up sections using methods that produce true alignment of axes without warp; use balanced welding sequences to minimise distortion.

Cut, drill or punch holes perpendicular to steel surfaces; flame cutting of holes and enlargement by burning is prohibited; any holes requiring enlargement must be reamed; drill holes in bearing plates only and remove burrs.
Holes required for other trades or for passage of services to be provided as shown on final approved shop drawings; coordinate hole locations to avoid unapproved field cutting.
Header units to be provided to support tail joists at openings in floor or roof systems unless otherwise indicated.
Develop required member cambers as indicated; where no camber is indicated, fabricate beams such that any natural camber is upward after erection.
Design and fabricate metal fabrications using material sizes, thicknesses and shapes indicated, and not less than necessary for performance requirements.
Form exposed fabricated work true to line and level, with accurate angles, flat surfaces and straight sharp edges; ease exposed edges to approximately 1 mm radius unless noted otherwise.
Shear and punch metals cleanly and accurately; remove burrs.
Remove sharp or rough areas on exposed traffic surfaces (e.g., stair treads, gratings).
Weld corners and seams continuously where specified, following EN 1011; form exposed connections with hairline joints flush and smooth.

Use concealed fasteners wherever possible for exposed work; where fasteners are exposed use Phillips flat-head (countersunk) screws or bolts unless otherwise indicated; locate joints least conspicuously.
Fabricate and space anchoring devices to provide adequate support for intended use; coordinate anchorage details with supporting structure.

Design fabrications planned for galvanizing to avoid risk of distortion (minimise unbalanced sections, avoid excessive jigging, use hot-rolled rather than cold-formed where possible, use balanced weld arrangements and uniform section thickness).

Provide adequate vent and drain holes for galvanizing, located and sized in accordance with good practice; consider single dipping of large items; splice oversized items where single dip is not feasible.

Maintain fabrication tolerances for metal fabrications: maximum squareness deviation 3 mm in diagonal, maximum offset between faces 2 mm, maximum misalignment of adjacent members 2 mm, maximum bow 3 mm in 1200 mm, maximum deviation from plane 2 mm in 1200 mm.
Prior to erection, Contractor to confirm anchor bolt alignment, elevation, projection and size; any inaccuracies or defects to be reported immediately.

At least 20 working days before steel erection, Contractor to survey existing location, alignment and elevation of anchor rods and notify Design Professionals of discrepancies; corrective measures, if required, must be performed before steel erection starts.
Steel erection to be executed in compliance with local best practice guidance and NBN EN 1090 tolerances; setting-out and construction tolerances stated as absolute, not additive.
Set structural frames accurately to lines and elevations indicated; align and adjust members forming part of complete frame before permanent fastening.
Clean bearing and contact surfaces before assembly; perform adjustments to compensate for discrepancies in alignment and level.
Allow for erection loads and provide sufficient temporary bracing to maintain structure in a safe condition, plumb and in true alignment until permanent bracing is installed.
Members may only be spliced where indicated on and accepted in shop drawings, or where subsequently agreed with Engineer of Record.
Do not enlarge unfair holes by burning or drift pins; ream holes that must be enlarged to admit bolts.

Gas cutting torches may not be used in the field to correct fabrication errors in structural framing without explicit acceptance from Engineer of Record; where permitted, gas-cut sections must have finish equal to sheared appearance.
No field cutting or altering of structural members without prior approval of Engineer of Record.
Steel erection must meet requirements of Execution Class 2 (EXC2) as stated in Section 2.6.J and NBN EN 1090-2.
The design assumes a minimum unrestrained temperature T0 = 10 °C for construction; Contractor must manage erection sequence and timing such that this assumption is met.
After erection, prime welds, abrasions and surfaces not shop-primed except surfaces to be in contact with concrete.
Grout to be solidly placed between column plates and bearing surfaces per manufacturer’s instructions for non-shrink grout; finished grout surfaces to be trowelled smooth and splayed to 45°.
Individual members of the steel structure must be level and plumb within EN 1090 tolerance limits.

Contractor is solely responsible for errors of detailing, fabrication and erection of structural steel and steel deck; conflicts and errors must be corrected at Contractor’s cost and without impact to project schedule where possible.
Install steel deck in accordance with manufacturer’s written recommendations, approved submittals and specified requirements.
Position deck units on supporting steel so that they are accurately aligned in final position with units resting tightly on top of supporting members.
Minimum bearing length of deck on steel supporting members shall be 50 mm.
Minimum roof deck end laps shall be 50 mm.
Roof deck to be wide rib units with no stiffening ribs on the top surface.
Cutting of deck to be neat and trim in appearance; cut using metal saw, drills or cutting torch while avoiding damage to adjacent steel.
Notch deck around columns and similar fabrications in a neat, controlled manner.
Cut holes and openings in deck only where indicated on Structural Drawings and approved submittals for field cutting.

Provide metal closures for openings in metal deck 1.58 mm wide and over, including cover plates for panel edges and ends and changes of direction, column closures between deck and columns, sheet metal collars at pipe and duct penetrations and ridge/valley plates to give acceptable surface for roofing.
No opening may be cut in metal decking unless shown on approved submittals or specifically approved in writing by the Engineer of Record.
For unplanned openings, Contractor must submit revised shop drawings and calculations for approval demonstrating compliance with all criteria.
Burning or weakening of deck material around welds is cause for rejection; deficient welds must be repaired or removed and replaced.

For composite deck: provide 20 mm diameter puddle welds at each end and intermediate supports of deck units, with maximum average spacing of 300 mm across deck width; puddle welds are not required where headed shear studs are welded through deck.
Longitudinal edges and side laps supported by steel members to be fastened with 20 mm diameter puddle welds at maximum 300 mm spacing along length.
Longitudinal side laps without steel support to be welded or fastened with minimum size self-tapping screws at maximum 150 mm spacing between supports; screws to be installed to maintain tight laps.
Longitudinal edge closures to be fastened by tack welding at maximum 600 mm spacing; sheet metal screws are not permitted for these closures.
Closures and accessories must be adequately connected to framing steel and adjacent deck units to ensure diaphragm continuity.

For non-composite deck: provide 20 mm puddle welds at ends and intermediate supports with maximum average spacing 200 mm across width; supported longitudinal edges and side laps to have 20 mm puddle welds at maximum 300 mm spacing along length; unsupported side laps to be welded or self-tapping screwed at maximum 150 mm spacing; longitudinal edge closures to be tack welded at maximum 150 mm spacing; sheet metal screws prohibited.
Alternative mechanical anchoring of metal deck (e.g., Hilti systems) may be used where supported by submitted and approved diaphragm calculations.
Welders performing deck welding to be certified by recognised authority in project location; welded connections to be visually inspected.

Shear studs to be welded through deck to primary steel members; top surface of beam must be free from mill scale, rust, grease, oil, paint and other contaminants before laying decking; studs must not be welded when ambient temperature is below 0 °C.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Temporary Support and Bracing – Structural Steel
tolerances_and_rules: The structural system shown on Contract Documents is designed to withstand design loads only when all structural elements are installed and fully connected.

Contractor’s Engineer is responsible for analysis of all components and assemblies for stresses and displacements induced by fabrication, shipping, handling, erection, temporary conditions and construction loads.
Contractor must provide sufficient temporary bracing and restraint during erection to maintain steelwork in a safe condition, plumb and true until permanent bracing is installed and complete.
Sequence of temporary works, including bracing locations and supports, must be documented in Temporary Works Drawings and Method Statements.
Temporary works must consider interaction with deck installation, cladding, precast elements and other structural components indicated to be supported by steel frame.
Contractor must not rely on SER for site safety programs or precautions; SER has no charge over safety programs at project site.
Verify field conditions are acceptable and ready to receive metal fabrications before installation; report discrepancies to A/E.
Clean and strip primed steel items to bare metal where site welding is required before welding operations.
Supply setting templates for steel items required to be cast into concrete or embedded in masonry to relevant trades.
Install metal fabrication items plumb and level, accurately fitted and free from distortion or defects.
Provide for erection loads and sufficient temporary bracing to maintain true alignment until permanent attachments are complete.
Perform field welding in accordance with EN 1011; weld only where indicated on drawings or approved in advance; obtain approval prior to site cutting or unscheduled adjustments.
After erection, prime welds, abrasions and surfaces that were not shop-primed or galvanized, except surfaces to be in contact with concrete.
Barrier rails to be temporarily supported plumb in each direction and cast integrally with monolithic footings where applicable.
Maintain fabrication tolerances during installation: maximum variation from plumb 6 mm and maximum offset from true alignment 6 mm for rails and similar items.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Metal Stairs, Ramps and Handrails Installation
tolerances_and_rules: Install stair and ramp components plumb and level, accurately fitted and free from distortion or defects.
Provide anchors, plates, angles, hangers and struts as required to connect stairs to the primary structure.
Allow for erection loads and provide temporary bracing to maintain alignment until permanent attachments are installed.
Provide welded site joints where specifically indicated on drawings; perform site welding in accordance with EN 1011.
Where not explicitly required to be welded, site joints may be either welded or bolted, provided jointing quality levels are maintained.
Mechanically fastened joints must be butted tight, flush and hairline; ground welds smooth and flush in exposed locations.
After erection, prime weld abrasions and surfaces not shop primed or galvanised, except surfaces that will be in direct contact with concrete.

Install steel pipe railings and handrails with posts spaced as indicated or as required by design loading; adjust railings prior to anchoring to ensure alignment at joints; plumb posts in each direction.
Anchor posts to steel by welding directly to steel supporting members.
Anchor wall-mounted handrail ends into concrete and masonry using steel round flanges welded to rail ends and drilled-in expansion anchors.
Secure handrails to walls using wall brackets and end fittings with minimum 50 mm clearance from wall to inside face of handrail; bracket spacing to support structural loads.

Use bracket types with flanges tapped for concealed anchorage to threaded hanger bolts; for concrete/solid masonry use drilled-in expansion anchors; for steel-framed gypsum board assemblies fasten brackets to steel framing or concealed anchors using self-tapping screws suited to loads.
Maximum variation from plumb for installed railings and handrails is 6 mm; maximum offset from true alignment is 6 mm.
Stair stringers to be rolled steel channels of 300 mm depth; flanges typically 75 mm where specified; landings to be same construction as treads and ramps and supported to meet design loads.
Stair towers at exit stairwells to be designed as self-supporting units stackable to building height.
Electrical platform stairs and landings to be fabricated with bolted connections that allow removal and replacement for equipment maintenance.
Roof stepover (bridge-style) stairs to be bigfoot-mounted and designed to resist height and wind loads per EN 14122.
Fixed ladders to be designed and installed in accordance with EN ISO 14122-4, including guardrails 1100 mm high, rung spacing 225–300 mm, maximum 6 m between landings, and safety hoops as specified.
Design clear widths, riser and going dimensions and pitch angle of stairs to meet or exceed all applicable local code requirements.

Design and fabricate stair assemblies, including stringers and landings, to support specified uniform and concentrated live loads with maximum deflection of stringer and landing framing limited to L/360.

Handrails and guardrails must be designed to withstand a uniform load of 1.0 kN/m applied in any direction at the top of guard top rail and a concentrated load of 0.5 kN applied at any point on top rail; concurrent action of uniform and point loads at top rail is not required.

Infill panels of guardrails must be designed to resist a horizontal uniform load of 1.0 kN/m² and a point load of 0.5 kN applied to infill; loads on infill do not have to act concurrently with loads on top rails.
Guardrail top rail nominal diameter to be 50 mm; handrail nominal diameter to be 32 mm; top rail height to meet local code requirements with minimum 1100 mm at landings.
Vertical picket infill spacing for guards not to exceed 100 mm centres; pickets to be 12.5 mm square solid bars welded top and bottom.
Pipe or tube rail infill elements to be sloped parallel to stair pitch and sized to meet load requirements.
Exposed edges and corners of metal stairs and ramps to be eased to uniform small radius; metal surfaces to be painted or galvanised to be sufficiently smooth for satin or matte finish.
Risers on stairs and ramps to be closed; nosings to have limited overhang and return per specified maximum dimensions.

Treads for grated stairs and ramps to be steel bar grating with minimum bearing bar depth 37.5 mm; open-grid configuration to meet local code opening requirements; nosings to be non-slip and contrasting in colour.
Install intumescent coatings only after verifying that steel members have been properly prepared, including use of compatible primers in good condition.
Provide enclosures as required to confine spraying operations, protect environment and maintain adequate ambient conditions for temperature, humidity, air quality and ventilation during application.
Clean steel substrates of all substances that could impair coating adhesion, including oil, grease, rolling compounds, incompatible primers, rust and mill scale.
Prime substrates with approved compatible primer unless an approved shop primer is already present and in satisfactory condition; ensure primers are fully cured before applying intumescent basecoats.
Protect coatings from rain, direct sunlight, high humidity and strong winds carrying dust or sand during application, drying and curing unless test evidence permits otherwise.
Do not apply additional coats until previous layers have fully cured as per manufacturer’s data sheets.

Comply strictly with manufacturer’s instructions for mixing, application and equipment selection; Contractor’s method statement and application practices must reflect conditions used in fire tests and assessments.
Apply primers, intumescent basecoats and top sealer coats to DFTs required to achieve specified fire resistance ratings, with DFTs defined in accordance with EN ISO 12944-5 for primer and topcoat.
Provide a uniform, defect-free finish matching approved mock-ups or samples in both appearance and thickness distribution.
DFT control is mandatory at multiple stages: measure and record primer DFT, intumescent basecoat DFT and final total DFT using appropriate gauges and survey procedures.
Average DFT applied to each element must be greater than or equal to specified nominal value.
Average measured DFT on any face of any member may not be less than 80% of the nominal value.
Values less than 80% of nominal are acceptable only if isolated and not exceeding 10% of readings on that member; minimum DFT must always be at least 50% of nominal.

Where a reading is below 80% of nominal, take additional readings within 150–300 mm of low reading; if all additional readings are at least 80% of nominal, the low reading can be considered isolated; otherwise, further readings are required to map the extent of under-thickness and additional coating must be applied before proceeding.
Average measured DFT of any face of any member must not exceed manufacturer’s recommended maximum thickness for that member shape and orientation.

Measurement frequencies: for I-sections, Tees and channels, take two readings per metre length on each face of web and outer faces of flanges plus one per metre on inner flange faces; for square/rectangular hollow sections and angles, take two readings per metre length on each face; for circular hollow sections, take eight readings per metre evenly distributed around the section.
For members less than 2 m in length, take three sets of readings (one at each end and one at centre) with numbers of readings per set as specified for section type.
Visual appearance of coatings to match specifications and approved samples; all defects or damage to coatings to be rectified and rechecked.

Special inspections and testing to be performed by independent testing agency as specified in Section 01 40 00; inspection scope includes surface preparation, environmental conditions during application, batch traceability, application times and compliance with recoat intervals.

qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Contractor must submit shop drawings for all individual structural steel shipping pieces produced in the fabrication shop, prepared and checked by a suitably qualified professional Structural Engineer. Erection drawings and method statements showing field installation and member placement, including connection locations, are required. Temporary works drawings and method statements prepared by the erector must show erection sequence, bracing locations, temporary supports and descriptions of bolting, welding and lifting procedures. Contractor must declare in writing that steel contains 70% recycled content (pre- and post-consumer) where achievable and copy submittals to EXE and DC Sustainability. If compliance with recycled content is not possible due to availability, schedule or cost, Contractor must submit a written exception request to the Engineer of Record with copies to EXE and DC Sustainability. Calculations for all connection designs must be submitted before preparation of shop drawings. A Quality Plan for execution of works in accordance with NBN EN 1090 must be submitted as early as possible after appointment.

Submit detailed shop drawings for steel deck showing type, identification mark, gauge, finish, locations, openings, dimensions, placement sequence, anchorage details, lap details, accessories, welding data, power requirements and electrode types. Show welding symbols in accordance with European Welding Association standards. Indicate locations of unframed openings, those to be cut after concrete placement and all deck closure and reinforcement details. Indicate type and location of inserts. Shop drawings for deck will not be reviewed without accompanying design calculations.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Shop Drawings – Metal Fabrications and Stairs
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Provide shop drawings for metal fabrications indicating profiles, sizes, connection attachments, reinforcing, anchorage, size and type of fasteners and accessories; include erection drawings, elevations and details as applicable. Use ISO 2553 or EN ISO 2553 welding symbols for welded connections and indicate net weld lengths. For metal stairs and ramps, shop drawings must show profiles, member sizes, connection attachments, reinforcement, anchorage, fasteners and accessories, with welded connections indicated using standard welding symbols and net weld lengths. Each sheet of stair shop drawings must bear the design engineer's signature.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Design Calculations – Structural Connections and Deck
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Submit design calculations for all steel connections not fully detailed in Contract Documents, prepared under the supervision of a Professional Structural Engineer experienced in structural steel design. Calculations must be clearly numbered in a logical system without renumbering on resubmittal and resubmissions indicated with an 'R' suffix; all changes must be clouded. Provide sketches for each calculation showing geometry and all relevant dimensions. For repetitive connections use summary tables and reference standard calculations. Provide drawing keys linking each connection to its calculation. All calculations must explicitly verify code requirements from NBN EN 1993 and loads shown on drawings; 'OK by inspection' is not acceptable. For steel decking, submit calculations for section properties for each deck type and gauge and calculations for slab edge and closure strips; these must be signed and sealed by a Professional Engineer specialising in structural engineering. Shop drawings for deck will not be reviewed without these calculations.

Submit manufacturer’s mill certificates for structural steel products, bolts, shear studs and other critical components, certifying that products meet or exceed specified standards (e.g., NBN EN 10025, NBN EN 10210, EN ISO 13918, EN ISO 898, NBN EN 1090). Material test reports must confirm mechanical and chemical properties in line with specified grades and codes.

Submit welder qualification certificates for all welders employed on structural steel and deck work, verifying qualification in accordance with NBN EN ISO 9606-1 within the previous 12 months. For deck welding, maintain records of welder qualification data and qualify welders through tests prescribed in European Welding Association standard qualification procedures and relevant standards. Where stricter requirements do not exist, each welder must prepare two specimens of each weld type; these specimens must be inspected, tested and approved by an independent Inspection and Testing Agency before the welder is allowed to work on the structure. Welding operators and weld setters for mechanized/automatic welding must be qualified to NBN EN ISO 14732 where applicable.

Structural steel fabricators must operate in accordance with all relevant EN codes and national annexes, and must hold CE Marking accreditation for the execution class relevant to the project (EXC2). Confirmation of membership in national Constructional Steelwork Associations or equivalent organisations must be provided. Metal fabrications must be produced by a fabricator experienced in similar work with sufficient capacity to meet project schedule. Stair fabricators must have a record of successful in-service performance of similar steel stairs. Intumescent coating installers must be certified or qualified by the coating manufacturer and trained directly by manufacturer employees. Intumescent coating manufacturers must maintain local direct technical staff able to attend site, including for start of installation.

Contractor must prepare and implement a Quality Plan for execution of structural steel works in accordance with NBN EN 1090, addressing fabrication, erection, welding, bolting, corrosion protection and inspection. All work must follow this Quality Plan. Temporary works, connection design and detailing workshops, pre-construction and pre-erection conferences must be documented and minutes issued within specified timeframes, but these meetings and associated documents are not substitutes for formal submittals and approvals.

Submit product data sheets for each intumescent coating system, including primers and topcoats. Provide test results from independent fire test laboratories based on EN 13381-4, including assessments used to determine required DFTs over the full range of section sizes. Assessments must be issued through an organisation subscribing to the Passive Fire Protection Federation’s 'Guide to Undertaking Assessments in Lieu of Fire Tests'. Submit product certificates from the manufacturer demonstrating compatibility of intumescent coatings with primers, adhesives and other coatings present on the steel. Submit tables or printouts of steel section factors versus required DFT for each product type to demonstrate satisfaction of fire ratings indicated on drawings.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Pre-Construction and Coordination Meetings – Structural Steel
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: At least 14 days before structural steel erection, Contractor must conduct a pre-construction conference to review quality control, construction requirements, submittal status, material availability, schedule, and inspection/testing procedures. Representatives required include Construction Manager, Contractor’s Site Engineer, Special Inspection and Testing Agency, structural steel detailer, fabricator, erector, Engineer of Record and Architect (if required). Contractor must record, type and distribute minutes within 5 days to Owner’s Representative, Architect and Engineer of Record. Contractor must notify external parties at least 7 days before the meeting. Failure to organise or document the meeting as required will be regarded as poor attention to specification and quality procedures. The meeting is not a substitute for formal submittals and approvals; comments by A/E or SER at the meeting are not binding.

At least 20 working days before steel erection commences, Contractor must hold a pre-erection conference to review detailed steel erection requirements. Attendees must include General Contractor/Construction Manager, Steel Erector/Fabricator, Erector’s Surveyor, Roof Deck Contractor, all Testing and Inspection Agencies, Design Professionals, Owner and Precast/Cladding Contractor as appropriate. Contractor must prepare an agenda, record and type minutes, and distribute them to all parties within 5 working days. Minutes must include detailed erection procedure, schedule of milestone dates for surveys and sign-offs on erection stages, surveying program and submission schedule for approval. SER is explicitly not responsible for site safety programs despite participation. Meeting organisation and compliance responsibilities rest solely with the Contractor, and the meeting does not replace formal approvals.

At least 20 working days before starting connection design and detailing, Fabricator must hold a workshop to confirm connection design assumptions and procedures and shop drawing preparation/submittal procedures. Contractor must prepare an agenda and require attendance from General Contractor, Fabricator, Detailer, Connection Engineer, Engineer of Record and Erector. Fabricator must prepare minutes and distribute to all attendees within 5 working days. Responsibility for organising and documenting the workshop lies entirely with the Contractor; failure to comply indicates poor attention to quality procedures. The workshop does not substitute for formal submittals and approvals and cannot be used to obtain approvals; A/E comments at the workshop are non-binding.

At least 14 days before application of intumescent coatings, Contractor must conduct a pre-construction meeting to review quality control and construction requirements, including submittal status, coordination with other trades, material availability, schedule and inspection/testing procedures. Required attendees include Construction Manager, Contractor’s Site Engineer, Special Inspection and Testing Agency, Fireproofing Applicator, Engineer of Record and Architect (if required). Contractor must record, type and distribute minutes within 5 days to Owner’s Representative, Architect and A/E of Record, and must notify external parties at least 7 days in advance.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Field Quality Control – Structural Steel and Deck
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: An independent testing agency must perform field quality control tests for structural steel erection and deck installation as specified in Section 01 40 00. Testing must include verification of high-strength bolted connections (e.g., tension verification or turn-of-nut inspections), visual inspection of all field-welded connections, and any additional nondestructive examination required by codes or project documents. Re-inspection is required for all failed tests at no cost or time delay to the Owner. For deck welding, visual inspection of puddle welds, edge welds and stud welds is required to verify conformance with spacing, size and quality requirements; deficient welds must be repaired or replaced and re-inspected.

An independent testing agency must conduct field quality control for intumescent coatings under Section 01 40 00, including verification of surface preparation standards (typically EN ISO 8501-1) and surface profile limits (EN ISO 8503-2); visual or EN ISO 8502-3 assessment of dust and contamination; verification of air and substrate temperatures, relative humidity and dew point during application; documentation of batch numbers, application dates/times and adherence to over-coating intervals; wet film thickness checks; and dry film thickness surveys at primer, basecoat and final stages. DFT data must be recorded systematically per member and face, and acceptance criteria regarding average and minimum thickness, isolated low readings and maximum thickness must be applied as specified. Visual finish must be checked against approved samples.

Drawings, construction agreement and Division 01 sections apply to all relevant sections. Section 01 40 00 governs quality requirements, testing and inspection. Contractor is responsible for examining work by others prior to starting steel installation and for checking dimensions and coordination between structural steel and other trades; commencement of work implies acceptance of preparatory work. Contractor must not rely on pre-construction or pre-erection meetings as substitutes for required submittals and formal approvals; any comments by A/E or SER during meetings do not override later formal reviews or relieve Contractor of responsibility.
